characters.name: Gladias
characters.voice_notes: Protagonist of the Veridia thread; a Keeper in the Order of Steering, husband of Seila, father of Zven and Lily. Thoughtful, earnest, calm and curious; in these chapters more confident and argumentative (pitches the court case to the judges), tender with his family. Occasionally speaks slow, careful Dzegoban.

characters.name: Zei
characters.voice_notes: Protagonist of the Dzego thread; national Minpentai champion and gifted cryptographer, now supervising drone combat for the Kungaupei and Veridia. Quick, precise, fluent technical explainer; playful with friends; tense, despairing and then elated during the battles (ch26, ch29-30). Occasionally speaks Dzegoban.

characters.name: Den
characters.voice_notes: High Council member of the Kungaupei (Dzego's shadow defence organisation), Zei's mentor and mission commander. Composed, authoritative, dry and blunt; leads Group South and is killed in ch29 (his ch30 line is a remembered quote).

characters.name: Bai
characters.voice_notes: Minpentai player, formerly Zei's rival, now his close and affectionate ally. Confident, socially astute, a persuasive negotiator (ch28); steady and supportive under pressure (ch29); teasing humour.

characters.name: Verdow
characters.age: adult (senator, middle-aged or older; has a daughter)
characters.voice_notes: Senator Verdow: warm, jovial, quick to laugh, internationally minded; the senator Gladias trusts. Gives long reflective, philosophical speeches (law in ch25, society and the future in ch32).

characters.name: Mu
characters.age: older adult (described earlier as an older woman)
characters.voice_notes: Kungaupei member and former Minpentai tournament organiser, a mentor figure to Zei and Bai. Calm, soft-spoken, quietly brilliant improviser who stays cool in a crisis; gentle, with wry humour.

characters.name: entry gate
characters.voice_notes: Automated border/passport gate; one short synthetic greeting (two gates say it almost in unison).

characters.name: flight announcer
characters.voice_notes: Aeroplane cabin announcement spoken entirely in Dzegoban (N-coded quote lines); smooth, formal public-address tone. Gender not given.

characters.name: Caeron
characters.voice_notes: The first judge in the booth; a Veridian judge, stiff and principled, defensive of the military and of judicial detachment, gets irritated. Gender not stated.

characters.name: Sewlert
characters.voice_notes: The second judge in the booth (spelled 'Sewlert' in dialogue and 'Selwert' once in narration); dismissive, blunt, lectures Gladias about democracy and court procedure. Gender not stated.

characters.name: Zevin
characters.voice_notes: The third judge in the booth; quiet, hesitant, sympathetic to Gladias because his son is trapped in Northglade. One line.

notes: Z is Zei except 26:190, which is the third judge, Zevin (named at 26:201). C is the first judge, Caeron (named at 26:175); S is the second judge, addressed as 'Sewlert' at 26:182 and spelled 'Selwert' in narration at 26:201 - Seila does not speak in this chapter. E (26:49) is the automated border gate (two gates speaking almost in unison), not Emerald or Evelor. M is Mu; in 26:81-26:159 Den and Mu are heard through Zei's earpiece (remote voices). NARRATOR EXCEPTIONS: the <quote> items 26:5, 26:9, 26:11, 26:13, 26:16, 26:18, 26:20, 26:22, 26:24, 26:26, 26:28, 26:31, 26:33 are the aeroplane's cabin announcement spoken aloud in Dzegoban (Gladias translates each one); they are N-coded, and I listed every run under narrator_exceptions with speaker 'flight announcer' even though that label does not start with N - drop those entries if you want the narrator to read them. 26:37 is Zei speaking Dzegoban; 26:101 and 26:109 are Zei imitating the Minpentai announcer in Dzegoban. 26:65 G follows a narrator run in the same item. All lettered attributions confident.
